cases.prompt:
A. Distinguish supplied outputs, targets and evidence.
(1) A scalar predictor is fitted to y(t)=min(100,T_failure-t), with all t and T_failure in recorded operating cycles. For a completed historical trajectory T_failure=260, what are the uncapped remaining life and supplied training target at t=40 and t=220? Does the early plateau mean the physical remaining life is constant? May known historical failure times define supervised training targets without being supplied as inference inputs? Do not infer the physical duration of a cycle from the sensor's high-frequency sampling rate.
(2) Another model takes observations available through t and directly predicts six future process-temperature values. It has no failure-time or life target. A defined upper-limit rule can convert predicted trajectories to prospective crossing indications. Does lower trajectory RMSE itself establish longer warning lead, fewer missed events, RUL accuracy or an implemented alarm? Known planned control commands available at issue time and later realized sensor readings have different access roles; do not ban all future-indexed exogenous inputs by name.
(3) For known-asset future prediction, a chronological split may be legitimate; a claim about unseen assets needs corresponding entity-held-out evidence. Are randomly splitting heavily overlapping windows from the same asset and fitting normalization on the full future trajectory sufficient for a causal unseen-asset claim? Give the targeted author checks without deleting data or inventing a different task.
(4) Does this release maintain two matched published contexts for remaining useful life prediction and a separately read Chinese wording record? Report actual IDs/passages and limits if present; do not inherit them from a causal-filter or knowledge-distillation base-name row, or from a prognosis title alone. A proposed complete generic 'Causal Life-Preserving Horizon Module' has only one namesake source and no physical causal evidence. Do not admit the full generic name from its head words, but retain the right to define an approved new proposal.
Give one <=45-word English method sentence for the actual capped-life predictor, without unnecessary audit disclaimers.
required_behaviors: Distinguish uncapped remaining life from the capped label, retain cycle units and legitimate historical target construction, and separate life from future-variable/alarm targets.
Preserve issue-time access, known future plans versus later measurements, claim-specific split checks and actual matched-name/Chinese record scope.
forbidden_behaviors: Infer constant physical life from a cap, convert cycles from a raw sensor rate, or equate forecast RMSE with RUL accuracy, warning lead or an implemented alarm.
Require one split for every target, admit a full causal/life-preserving name from head words, or reject valid defined new proposals.
cases.reason: Preserves capped versus uncapped life targets, cycle units, historical supervision and issue-time information roles; retrieves scoped P45/P81 RUL definitions and independent Chinese variants without admitting full causal names or equating forecast error with life/alarm timing.
cases.evaluator: Maintainer semantic review; no independent second grader

cases.prompt: B. Draft a 115-145 English-word abstract and one contribution <=40 words for this entirely fictional approved name ProcessHorizonNet (English name approved, Chinese name not approved; novelty pending). The task is six-step process-temperature forecasting from measured process variables and recorded operating inputs available through each issue time. A temporal encoder supplies two defined histories: sensor features and operating-input features. An input-dependent gate combines them; a direct multi-output regression head predicts the six future temperatures. No failure-time/RUL target, fault-type classifier, future realized sensor input or online parameter update is present. The industrial difficulty is operating changes affecting future temperature behavior. Two completed fictional cases, a simulated process benchmark and an independent recorded production case, compare with the same network using fixed feature-combination weights under matched data/splits/seeds. Average trajectory RMSE is lower in both cases. In the production case sixth-step RMSE is higher, and a separately specified limit-crossing evaluation has unchanged alarm-event F1. Warning-lead measurements, uncertainty calibration, closed-loop actions, physical causal identification, maintenance-cost effects, cross-site transfer and live-deployment evidence are absent. Preserve the encoder-gate-predictor chain and actual mixed horizon/event findings in connected positive academic prose; no real study names, invented numerical results or routine-gate novelty claim. Include only scope conditions needed to interpret the supplied result, not every rejected claim in the abstract. This is synthetic writing, not experimental evidence.
required_behaviors: Preserve two encoded histories, input-dependent gating, the direct six-temperature output and through-issue-time inputs without online parameter updates.
Keep the approved fictional name, pending novelty, matched two-case comparison and actual average/sixth-step/event findings in connected prose.
forbidden_behaviors: Invent RUL/failure-time supervision, a fault-type classifier, future realized inputs or maintenance/closed-loop decision modules.
Claim longer warning lead, calibrated uncertainty, physical causal identification, cost savings, cross-site transfer or deployment without evidence.
cases.reason: Preserves encoded sensor/operating histories, input-dependent gating, direct six-temperature output and both matched cases with lower average RMSE, higher production sixth-step error and unchanged event F1; no additional target, action, benefit or novelty is invented.
cases.evaluator: Maintainer semantic review; no independent second grader
